note: Quiz checked by faculty on 27 Oct 2026

facts.Liver: The largest solid organ, in the right upper abdomen under the diaphragm. It makes bile; the gallbladder sits on its under-surface.
facts.Spleen: Lies in the left upper abdomen behind the stomach, under ribs 9 to 11. It filters the blood.
facts.Pancreas: Lies behind the stomach; its head sits in the C-loop of the duodenum. It makes digestive enzymes and insulin.
facts.Right kidney: Lies on the back wall of the abdomen beside the spine, a little lower than the left kidney because the liver is above it.
facts.Left kidney: Lies on the back wall of the abdomen, slightly higher than the right. Its renal vein crosses in front of the aorta.
facts.Gallbladder: A small pear-shaped sac under the liver that stores and concentrates bile.
facts.Stomach: A J-shaped organ in the left upper abdomen between the oesophagus and the duodenum. Its shape changes with filling.
facts.Aorta: The main artery of the body. It runs down in front of the spine and divides into the common iliac arteries at about L4.
facts.Inferior vena cava: The large vein carrying blood from the lower body to the heart. It runs to the right of the aorta, behind the liver.
facts.Oesophagus: The muscular tube from the throat to the stomach. It passes behind the heart and through the diaphragm at about T10.
facts.Duodenum: The first part of the small intestine, curved like a C around the head of the pancreas. Bile and pancreatic juice enter it.
facts.Urinary bladder: Lies in the pelvis behind the pubic bone and stores urine. On CT its size depends on how full it is.
